edit.title: Edit
edit.description: Image feature editing is a sophisticated geometric manipulation operation that allows users to modify and enhance specific features within digital images. The operation takes input in the form of source images in various formats (JPEG, PNG, TIFF) along with precise parameters for feature selection and modification values. The output is a transformed image with altered geometric characteristics based on the specified edits. Key parameters include feature selection tools, transformation matrices, and geometric constraints that control how the modifications are applied. This fundamental operation finds extensive applications across multiple domains, including professional photo editing software, architectural visualization tools, computer-aided design systems, and digital art creation platforms. It enables users to perform precise adjustments to lines, shapes, proportions, and specific image elements while maintaining image quality and spatial relationships.

crop.title: Crop
crop.description: Image cropping is a fundamental image processing operation that extracts a specific region of interest from a larger source image. The operation requires an input image in any standard digital format and precise coordinates defining the crop region through parameters like starting point (x, y coordinates), width, and height of the desired area. Additional parameters may include aspect ratio constraints and edge smoothing options. The operation outputs a new image containing only the selected portion, preserving the original resolution within the cropped area. Cropping finds extensive applications in professional photography for composition improvement, document processing for isolating relevant content, medical imaging for focusing on specific anatomical regions, web design for content optimization, and social media platforms for thumbnail generation. It's essential in workflows requiring precise image area selection and content focusing.

flip.title: Flip
flip.description: Image flipping is a geometric transformation operation that creates a mirror reflection of the input image either horizontally or vertically. The operation accepts any standard image format as input and requires parameters specifying the flip axis (horizontal or vertical) and optional border handling methods. The output is a transformed image where all pixels are reversed along the specified axis, maintaining the original image's dimensions and quality. This operation is particularly useful in various applications, including professional photography for creative effects, medical imaging for standardizing view orientations, printing industry for transfer applications, computer vision for data augmentation in machine learning, and quality control processes in manufacturing. Flipping also serves as a correction tool for images captured through mirrors or specialized optical systems.

rotate.title: Rotate
rotate.description: Image rotation is a geometric transformation operation that changes the orientation of an image by rotating it around a specified point, typically the center. The input parameters include the source image, rotation angle in degrees (positive or negative), rotation center coordinates, and interpolation method for pixel resampling. Optional parameters control background fill color and border handling. The operation outputs a transformed image with all pixels rotated by the specified angle, potentially with different dimensions to accommodate the rotated content. This operation is fundamental in various applications, including automated document processing for orientation correction, medical imaging for standardizing anatomical views, satellite image processing for geographic alignment, professional photography for composition adjustment, and manufacturing quality control for object alignment verification.

resize.title: Resize
resize.description: Image resizing is a crucial operation that modifies the dimensions of a digital image while managing its visual content. The operation accepts input images in any standard format and requires parameters for target dimensions (width and height), scaling method (uniform or non-uniform), and interpolation algorithm (nearest neighbor, bilinear, bicubic). Additional parameters control aspect ratio preservation and anti-aliasing settings. The output is a transformed image matching the specified dimensions while maintaining optimal visual quality. Resizing is extensively used in web development for responsive design, digital publishing for multi-platform content delivery, social media for thumbnail generation, video processing for resolution standardization, and e-commerce platforms for product image optimization. The operation balances quality preservation with size requirements.

smart_resize.title: Smart Resize
smart_resize.description: Smart resize is an advanced image processing operation that intelligently modifies image dimensions while preserving critical visual content and structural elements. The operation takes an input image and target dimensions, utilizing sophisticated content-aware algorithms to analyze and protect important image features. Key parameters include content importance weights, structure preservation thresholds, and scaling constraints. The operation produces a resized image that maintains visual integrity of key elements while adapting to new dimensions. This technology finds critical applications in responsive web design for automatic image adaptation, digital publishing platforms for dynamic content scaling, professional photography for selective resizing, user interface design for multi-device optimization, and automated media processing systems. It significantly improves upon traditional resizing methods through intelligent content analysis.

correct_perspective.title: Correct Perspective
correct_perspective.description: Perspective correction is a sophisticated image transformation operation that removes geometric distortion caused by camera angle and position relative to the subject. The operation requires an input image and perspective control points or planes, along with parameters for transformation intensity and interpolation method. Additional parameters control grid density, boundary handling, and output dimension constraints. The resulting image shows the subject as if photographed perpendicular to its principal plane, with parallel lines preserved. This operation is crucial in architectural photography for building rectification, document digitization for accurate text reproduction, forensic image analysis for measurement accuracy, product photography for standardized views, and computer vision applications for geometric normalization. It enables accurate measurements and improved visual presentation of photographed objects.

deinterlace.title: Deinterlace
deinterlace.description: Deinterlacing is a specialized video processing operation that converts interlaced video frames into progressive ones by handling odd and even fields. The operation takes interlaced video frames as input, requiring parameters for field order (top/bottom field first), motion detection thresholds, and interpolation method selection. Additional parameters control artifact reduction and output frame rate handling. The operation produces progressive frames without the visual artifacts associated with interlacing. This process is essential in digital video processing workflows, particularly in broadcast technology for format conversion, DVD and Blu-ray authoring for optimal playback quality, video streaming platforms for content optimization, and legacy video restoration projects. It significantly improves visual quality for modern display systems.

field_shift.title: Field Shift
field_shift.description: Field shift is a specialized video processing operation that aligns the two fields of an interlaced video frame to correct temporal misalignment issues. The operation accepts interlaced video frames as input, with parameters controlling field timing offset, motion compensation settings, and pixel interpolation methods. Additional parameters manage artifact suppression and edge handling. The output is a frame with properly aligned fields, reducing motion artifacts and improving overall visual quality. This operation is particularly important in broadcast video processing for quality control, digital archive restoration for preserving legacy content, sports video analysis for precise motion study, and video format conversion workflows. It helps maintain temporal accuracy in interlaced video content.

undistort.title: Undistort
undistort.description: Undistort is a complex image correction operation that compensates for optical distortions introduced by camera lenses, particularly in wide-angle and zoom lenses. The operation requires an input image and lens calibration parameters, including distortion coefficients and camera matrix values. Additional parameters control correction intensity and border handling methods. The output is an image with straight lines restored and geometric distortions minimized. This operation is essential in professional photography for architectural shots, computer vision systems for accurate measurements, photogrammetry applications for 3D reconstruction, quality control systems in manufacturing, and scientific imaging where geometric accuracy is crucial. It ensures geometric fidelity in captured images.

correct_aspect_ratio.title: Correct Aspect Ratio
correct_aspect_ratio.description: Aspect ratio correction is a video processing operation that adjusts the proportions of video frames to ensure proper display geometry. The operation takes video frames as input, with parameters specifying the target aspect ratio, scaling method, and pixel aspect ratio handling. Additional parameters control letterboxing/pillarboxing options and resolution management. The output is a frame with corrected proportions that maintains proper visual appearance across different display systems. This operation is crucial in broadcast video production for format standardization, film-to-video conversion projects, streaming media platforms for multi-device compatibility, DVD authoring for proper playback, and digital restoration of legacy content. It ensures consistent visual presentation across different display formats.

interleave.title: Interleave
interleave.description: Interleave is a specialized video processing operation that combines separate video fields into standard interlaced video format. The operation takes progressive video frames or separate fields as input, requiring parameters for field order specification, temporal alignment settings, and artifact reduction controls. Additional parameters manage motion handling and edge treatment. The output is properly interlaced video frames suitable for broadcast or legacy video systems. This operation is vital in professional video production workflows, particularly in broadcast television for format compliance, video archiving for legacy format preservation, sports replay systems for slow-motion analysis, and video format conversion processes. It ensures compatibility with interlaced video systems while maintaining visual quality.

correct_fisheye.title: Correct Fisheye
correct_fisheye.description: Fisheye correction is an advanced image processing operation that compensates for the extreme wide-angle distortion characteristic of fisheye lenses. The input includes the distorted image and specific lens parameters such as field of view, distortion coefficients, and optical center coordinates. Additional parameters control correction strength and output projection type. The operation produces a rectilinear image where straight lines in the scene appear straight in the final image. This correction is crucial in architectural photography for accurate building documentation, surveillance systems for proper scene analysis, virtual reality content creation for immersive experiences, and scientific applications requiring accurate geometric measurements. It enables practical use of ultra-wide-angle imagery.

unroll.title: Unroll
unroll.description: Unroll is a specialized image processing operation that transforms omnidirectional or 360-degree images into flat panoramic representations. The operation takes spherical or cylindrical image projections as input, with parameters controlling output projection type, sampling density, and coordinate mapping methods. Additional parameters manage seam handling and perspective correction. The output is a standard panoramic image suitable for conventional viewing methods. This operation finds extensive applications in virtual tour creation for real estate and tourism, surveillance system monitoring, immersive content production for virtual reality, architectural documentation for complete space visualization, and scientific imaging for comprehensive environmental analysis. It makes 360-degree content accessible in traditional viewing formats.

grayscale_conversion.title: Grayscale Conversion
grayscale_conversion.description: Grayscale conversion is a fundamental image processing operation that transforms color images into monochrome representations by calculating luminance values. The operation takes a color image input in any standard format and requires parameters for conversion method selection (average, weighted, or luminance-preserving algorithms) and output bit depth specification. Additional parameters control gamma correction and contrast preservation. The resulting image contains only intensity information, with each pixel represented by a single value indicating brightness. This operation is crucial in medical imaging for X-ray and MRI visualization, document processing for text extraction, computer vision for feature detection, security systems for facial recognition, and scientific analysis where color information is not relevant. It simplifies image analysis and reduces computational requirements.

color_conversion.title: Color Conversion
color_conversion.description: Color conversion is a sophisticated image processing operation that transforms images between different color spaces while preserving visual information. The operation accepts grayscale or color images as input, requiring parameters for target color space specification (RGB, HSV, LAB, etc.), conversion matrix coefficients, and gamut mapping methods. Additional parameters manage color profile handling and quantization settings. The output is an image represented in the desired color space with appropriate channel values. This operation is essential in professional printing for color accuracy, digital photography for creative effects, medical imaging for tissue analysis, scientific visualization for data representation, and quality control in manufacturing. It ensures accurate color reproduction across different devices and applications.

color_switch.title: Color Switch
color_switch.description: Color switching is a specialized image processing operation that exchanges color channels within an image, typically focusing on red and blue channel interchange. The input is a color image with parameters specifying which channels to swap, intensity preservation options, and gamma correction settings. Additional parameters control color balance adjustment and saturation preservation. The output is an image with specified color channels interchanged while maintaining overall image structure. This operation finds applications in scientific imaging for fluorescence microscopy, medical imaging for tissue visualization, astronomical imaging for spectral analysis, art and design for creative effects, and color correction in video production. It enables specific color manipulation for both technical and artistic purposes.

extract_channel.title: Extract Channel
extract_channel.description: Channel extraction is a precise image processing operation that isolates a single color channel from a multi-channel image. The operation takes a color image input and parameters specifying the target channel (red, green, blue, hue, saturation, etc.), extraction method, and output format settings. Additional parameters control normalization, scaling, and contrast enhancement of the extracted channel. The output is a single-channel image representing the isolated component. This operation is crucial in medical imaging for specific tissue analysis, remote sensing for vegetation monitoring, document analysis for security features, quality control in printing, and scientific imaging for specific wavelength analysis. It enables detailed analysis of individual color components for specialized applications.

enable_channels.title: Enable Channels
enable_channels.description: Channel enabling is a selective image processing operation that controls the visibility and combination of color channels in multi-channel images. The operation takes a color image input with parameters for channel selection (which channels to display or hide), intensity scaling for each channel, and blending methods. Additional parameters manage color balance and gamma correction for visible channels. The output displays only the selected color channels while suppressing others. This operation is vital in fluorescence microscopy for multiple stain visualization, medical imaging for contrast enhancement, scientific visualization for data analysis, color proofing in printing, and professional photography for color correction. It allows precise control over color channel visualization.

contrast_and_brightness.title: Contrast and Brightness
contrast_and_brightness.description: Contrast and brightness adjustment is a fundamental image enhancement operation that modifies the dynamic range and overall luminance of an image. The operation accepts any standard image format as input, with parameters controlling contrast multiplication factor, brightness offset value, and preservation of color relationships. Additional parameters manage gamma correction, histogram stretching, and clipping prevention. The output is an image with modified tonal range and luminance values that improve visual clarity. This operation is essential in medical imaging for diagnostic clarity, photography post-processing, scientific visualization for data interpretation, video production for consistent appearance, and display system calibration. It enables basic but crucial image quality improvements for various applications.

exposure.title: Exposure
exposure.description: Exposure adjustment is a sophisticated image processing operation that compensates for improper camera exposure settings during image capture. The input image requires parameters for exposure value (EV) adjustment, highlight recovery settings, and shadow preservation controls. Additional parameters manage color balance maintenance, noise reduction in adjusted regions, and gamma correction. The output is an image with corrected exposure levels that better represent the original scene. This operation is crucial in professional photography for post-processing, forensic image analysis for detail recovery, digital archive restoration, real estate photography for interior/exterior balance, and scientific imaging where proper exposure is critical. It helps recover information from improperly exposed images.

hsv.title: Hue/Saturation/Value
hsv.description: HSV adjustment is a comprehensive color modification operation that independently controls the hue, saturation, and value components of an image. The operation takes a color image input with parameters for hue rotation angle, saturation scaling factor, and value adjustment range. Additional parameters manage color selective adjustments, gamut preservation, and smooth transitions between modified regions. The output is an image with modified color characteristics while maintaining natural appearance. This operation is essential in professional photography for color grading, video production for mood setting, digital art creation for stylistic effects, product photography for accurate color representation, and brand consistency in marketing materials. It provides precise control over color appearance.

curves.title: Curves
curves.description: Curves adjustment is a powerful image processing operation that enables precise control over tonal range and color balance through custom transfer functions. The operation accepts any image format and requires parameters for curve points in each channel, interpolation method, and output range mapping. Additional parameters control anchor point smoothing, histogram preservation, and selective adjustments. The output is an image with modified tonal values according to the specified curves. This operation is fundamental in professional photography for precise tonal control, color grading in film production, medical imaging for optimal visualization, scientific image analysis for data enhancement, and prepress workflow for print optimization. It offers sophisticated control over image tonality.

levels.title: Levels
levels.description: Levels adjustment is a comprehensive image processing operation that controls image tonality by manipulating input and output levels for shadows, midtones, and highlights. The operation takes any standard image format and requires parameters for black point, white point, and gamma values for each color channel. Additional parameters manage output level mapping and color preservation. The resulting image shows optimized tonal distribution with improved contrast and color balance. This operation is essential in professional photography for exposure correction, video post-production for consistent look, scientific imaging for data visualization, medical imaging for diagnostic clarity, and print production for optimal reproduction. It provides precise control over image tonal range.

histogram_equalization.title: Histogram Equalization
histogram_equalization.description: Histogram equalization is an adaptive image enhancement operation that improves contrast by redistributing pixel intensity values across the available range. The operation accepts grayscale or color images as input, with parameters controlling equalization method, clipping limits, and distribution mapping. Additional parameters manage channel-wise processing and local adaptation settings. The output is an image with enhanced contrast and improved detail visibility across all tonal regions. This operation is crucial in medical imaging for diagnostic clarity, satellite image processing for feature enhancement, microscopy for specimen analysis, security surveillance for detail visibility, and scientific visualization for data interpretation. It automatically optimizes image contrast for better visual analysis.

clahe.title: CLAHE
clahe.description: CLAHE (Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization) is an advanced image enhancement operation that improves local contrast while limiting noise amplification. The operation takes grayscale or color images as input, requiring parameters for tile size, contrast limit, and distribution shape. Additional parameters control interpolation method and edge handling at tile boundaries. The output shows enhanced local contrast with reduced noise artifacts compared to standard histogram equalization. This operation is particularly valuable in medical imaging for tissue visualization, aerial photography for terrain analysis, microscopy for cell structure examination, automotive vision systems for improved detection, and scientific imaging where local detail preservation is crucial. It provides superior contrast enhancement for complex images.

contrast_stretch.title: Contrast Stretch
contrast_stretch.description: Contrast stretching is an adaptive image enhancement operation that expands the range of intensity values to improve image visibility. The input image requires parameters for minimum and maximum percentile values, stretching method selection, and clipping threshold settings. Additional parameters control channel-wise processing and normalization methods. The output shows improved contrast with better utilization of the available dynamic range while preserving relative intensity relationships. This operation is essential in satellite image processing for feature visibility, medical imaging for tissue differentiation, microscopy for specimen analysis, industrial inspection for defect detection, and scientific visualization where optimal contrast is crucial. It enhances image readability while maintaining important visual relationships.

negative.title: Negative
negative.description: Negative transformation is a fundamental image processing operation that inverts pixel values to create a photographic negative effect. The operation accepts any standard image format as input, with parameters controlling inversion method, channel processing options, and output value mapping. Additional parameters manage gamma correction and color preservation in specific ranges. The output is an inverted image where light areas become dark and vice versa, while maintaining overall image structure. This operation finds applications in medical imaging for enhanced visualization, film processing for negative scanning, scientific imaging for feature highlighting, artistic effects in photography, and quality control in printing processes. It provides an alternative visualization that can reveal hidden details.

threshold.title: Threshold
threshold.description: Threshold is a binary image segmentation operation that separates image features based on intensity values. The operation accepts grayscale or color images as input, requiring parameters for threshold values (single or multiple levels), threshold method selection (global or local), and output value assignment. Additional parameters control adaptive threshold behavior and noise filtering options. The output is a binary or multi-level image where pixels are classified based on their relationship to threshold values. This operation is fundamental in document processing for text extraction, quality control for defect detection, medical imaging for tissue segmentation, computer vision for object detection, and scientific image analysis for feature isolation. It provides basic but crucial image segmentation capabilities.

adaptive_threshold.title: Adaptive Threshold
adaptive_threshold.description: Adaptive threshold is an advanced segmentation operation that automatically determines optimal threshold values for different image regions. The input image requires parameters for window size, adaptation method, sensitivity factor, and constant offset value. Additional parameters manage border handling and smoothing options for threshold transitions. The output is a binary image with locally optimized segmentation that adapts to varying image conditions. This operation is particularly valuable in document analysis for text extraction under varying illumination, microscopy for cell detection, quality inspection systems for defect identification, biometric systems for feature extraction, and computer vision applications requiring robust segmentation. It performs better than global thresholding in images with varying backgrounds.

laplace.title: Laplace
laplace.description: Laplace edge detection is a second-order differential operation that identifies rapid intensity changes in images. The operation takes grayscale images as input, with parameters specifying kernel size, normalization method, and edge enhancement factors. Additional parameters control noise suppression and output scaling. The resulting image highlights edges and fine details by detecting zero-crossings in the second derivative of intensity values. This operation is essential in medical imaging for boundary detection, microscopy for cell analysis, computer vision for feature extraction, quality control for defect detection, and scientific imaging for structure analysis. It provides detailed edge information but is sensitive to noise, making pre-processing often necessary.

sobel.title: Sobel
sobel.description: Sobel edge detection is a gradient-based operation that identifies image edges using first-order derivatives. The input is typically a grayscale image, with parameters controlling kernel direction (horizontal/vertical), gradient threshold values, and edge strength normalization. Additional parameters manage noise suppression and output format settings. The operation produces an image highlighting edges based on intensity gradients, with options for magnitude and direction information. This technique is widely used in machine vision for object detection, medical imaging for structure analysis, industrial inspection for defect identification, autonomous systems for navigation, and scientific imaging for feature extraction. It provides robust edge detection with good noise tolerance.

scharr.title: Scharr
scharr.description: Scharr operator is a specialized edge detection operation that provides improved rotational symmetry compared to Sobel filters. The operation accepts grayscale images as input, requiring parameters for gradient direction, threshold values, and output scaling methods. Additional parameters control preprocessing filters and edge enhancement settings. The output image shows enhanced edge detection with better accuracy for diagonal edges compared to traditional operators. This operation is crucial in computer vision applications requiring precise edge orientation, medical imaging for structure analysis, industrial inspection systems, scientific visualization of directional features, and pattern recognition tasks. It offers superior gradient estimation for critical applications.

canny.title: Canny
canny.description: Canny edge detection is a multi-stage operation that provides optimal edge detection through noise reduction and hysteresis thresholding. The input image requires parameters for Gaussian smoothing sigma, high and low threshold values, and edge linking criteria. Additional parameters manage non-maximum suppression and output format options. The operation produces a binary edge map with superior edge localization and minimal false detections. This advanced technique is essential in computer vision for feature extraction, medical imaging for boundary detection, industrial automation for part recognition, robotics for environment perception, and scientific imaging for structure analysis. It is considered the optimal edge detection method for many applications.

linear_filter.title: Linear Filter
linear_filter.description: Linear filtering is a versatile image processing operation that applies user-defined convolution kernels for various enhancement and analysis purposes. The operation takes any image type as input, with parameters specifying the kernel matrix values, normalization method, and border handling options. Additional parameters control filter response scaling and multi-pass applications. The output is a filtered image reflecting the specific characteristics of the applied kernel. This operation is fundamental in image enhancement for noise reduction, edge detection for feature extraction, texture analysis for pattern recognition, scientific imaging for specific feature highlighting, and signal processing applications. It provides customizable image transformation capabilities.

bilinear_filter.title: Bilinear Filter
bilinear_filter.description: Bilinear filtering is an advanced operation that combines the results of two separate linear filters to achieve complex image transformations. The input image requires parameters for two distinct kernel definitions, combination method selection, and weighting factors. Additional parameters manage individual filter responses and final output normalization. The operation produces a filtered image incorporating the combined effects of both kernels, enabling more sophisticated processing than single linear filters. This technique is valuable in texture analysis for pattern recognition, medical imaging for feature enhancement, scientific visualization for data analysis, industrial inspection for defect detection, and specialized image processing applications requiring complex filter responses.

channel_mixer.title: Channel Mixer
channel_mixer.description: Channel mixing is a sophisticated color manipulation operation that adjusts the contribution of each color channel to the final output channels. The input requires a color image and parameters specifying mixing coefficients for each output channel, preservation of overall intensity, and optional constant offsets. Additional parameters control gamut mapping and color space conversion settings. The output shows modified color relationships based on the specified channel mixing ratios. This operation is crucial in color correction for video production, scientific imaging for spectral analysis, medical imaging for tissue differentiation, photography for creative effects, and color management systems for precise color control. It enables complex color transformations while maintaining image integrity.

color_deconvolution.title: Color Deconvolution
color_deconvolution.description: Color deconvolution is an advanced image analysis operation that separates and enhances specific color components based on their spectral characteristics. The operation takes color images as input, requiring parameters for target color vectors, separation matrix calculation, and output scaling methods. Additional parameters manage noise suppression and component normalization. The resulting images show maximized differences between specified colors, particularly useful in biological stain separation. This operation is essential in medical microscopy for stain analysis, histology for tissue examination, biological research for cell identification, material science for composition analysis, and quality control applications requiring precise color separation.

component_separation.title: Component Separation
component_separation.description: Component separation is an analytical image processing operation that isolates distinct informative elements within complex images. The input image requires parameters for separation method selection, component identification criteria, and output format specifications. Additional parameters control noise handling and component enhancement settings. The operation produces separate images highlighting different information-bearing components present in the original image. This technique is crucial in medical imaging for tissue classification, remote sensing for land use analysis, document processing for feature extraction, scientific imaging for data interpretation, and quality control systems for material analysis. It enables detailed examination of specific image components.

fourier.title: Fourier
fourier.description: Fourier transform processing is a sophisticated operation that analyzes and modifies images in the frequency domain to remove periodic noise and interference patterns. The input image requires parameters for transform type selection, frequency filter definitions, and inverse transform settings. Additional parameters manage window functions and output normalization. The operation produces images with reduced periodic artifacts and enhanced signal components through frequency domain manipulation. This advanced technique is essential in scientific imaging for interference removal, medical imaging for artifact reduction, astronomical imaging for noise suppression, industrial inspection for pattern analysis, and microscopy for image enhancement. It enables powerful frequency-based image processing capabilities.

measure_1d.title: Measure 1D
measure_1d.description: One-dimensional measurement is a fundamental image processing operation that extracts linear distances from planar images. The operation requires an input image with calibration markers or known reference dimensions, parameters for scale factor calculation, measurement unit specification, and pixel-to-real-world conversion settings. Additional parameters control perspective distortion compensation and measurement accuracy estimation. The output provides real-world distance measurements along with uncertainty values. This operation is essential in medical imaging for anatomical measurements, industrial quality control for part dimensioning, construction documentation for distance verification, forensic analysis for crime scene investigation, and scientific research for object sizing. It enables non-contact measurement capabilities for applications requiring linear dimensional analysis.

measure_2d.title: Measure 2D
measure_2d.description: Two-dimensional measurement is an advanced image processing operation that extracts planar measurements after correcting for perspective distortion. The input image requires camera calibration data, perspective correction parameters, and reference dimension information. Additional parameters manage surface plane definition, distortion compensation, and measurement accuracy verification. The output provides real-world measurements in two dimensions with associated uncertainty estimates. This operation is crucial in architectural documentation for floor plan verification, industrial inspection for component sizing, aerial photography for land surveying, forensic analysis for scene reconstruction, and quality control applications requiring area measurements. It enables accurate dimensional analysis of objects in non-perpendicular views.

measure_3d.title: Measure 3D
measure_3d.description: Three-dimensional measurement is a sophisticated image processing operation that extracts spatial measurements using 3D reconstruction models. The operation requires multiple input images or depth data, camera calibration parameters, and 3D model reconstruction settings. Additional parameters control point cloud generation, surface modeling, and measurement accuracy validation. The output provides real-world measurements in three dimensions with comprehensive uncertainty analysis. This operation is vital in industrial metrology for complex part inspection, medical imaging for volumetric analysis, architectural documentation for building surveys, archaeological documentation for artifact measurement, and scientific research requiring precise 3D dimensional analysis. It enables comprehensive spatial measurement capabilities from image-based data.

laplacian_sharpening.title: Laplacian Sharpening
laplacian_sharpening.description: Laplacian sharpening is a detail enhancement operation that uses second-order derivatives to accentuate edge features. The operation takes any standard image format as input, requiring parameters for kernel size, sharpening intensity, and edge enhancement threshold. Additional parameters manage noise suppression and output blending options. The resulting image shows improved edge definition and local contrast while controlling noise amplification. This operation is fundamental in medical imaging for structure enhancement, microscopy for detail visualization, professional photography for creative sharpening, scientific imaging for feature highlighting, and quality control systems for defect detection. It provides effective detail enhancement through edge accentuation.

unsharp_masking.title: Unsharp Masking
unsharp_masking.description: Unsharp masking is a sophisticated sharpening operation that enhances edges by subtracting a blurred version from the original image. The input image requires parameters for blur radius, sharpening amount, and threshold values for detail discrimination. Additional parameters control mask generation and final image blending. The output shows enhanced local contrast and edge definition while maintaining natural appearance. This operation is essential in professional photography for detail enhancement, medical imaging for diagnostic clarity, printing preparation for optimal reproduction, scientific visualization for feature emphasis, and video post-production for improved detail visibility. It offers controlled sharpening with minimal artifacts.

averaging_filter.title: Averaging Filter
averaging_filter.description: Averaging filter is a basic noise reduction operation that smooths images through local mean calculation. The input image requires parameters for kernel size, edge preservation threshold, and iteration count settings. Additional parameters control weight distribution and boundary handling methods. The output shows reduced random noise with some softening of image details. This operation is useful in medical imaging for noise reduction, scientific data analysis for signal smoothing, industrial inspection for pattern enhancement, preprocessing for feature detection, and general image quality improvement. It provides simple but effective noise reduction for images with moderate noise levels.

gaussian_filter.title: Gaussian Filter
gaussian_filter.description: Gaussian filtering is a sophisticated smoothing operation that reduces noise while preserving edge structure through weighted averaging. The input image requires parameters for sigma value (blur radius), kernel size, and border handling method. Additional parameters control separable filtering options and output normalization. The resulting image shows reduced noise with better detail preservation compared to simple averaging. This operation is essential in medical imaging for noise suppression, computer vision for preprocessing, scientific imaging for data smoothing, photography for noise reduction, and feature detection applications. It provides effective noise reduction with controlled detail loss.

bilateral_filter.title: Bilateral Filter
bilateral_filter.description: Bilateral filtering is an advanced edge-preserving smoothing operation that combines domain and range filtering. The input image requires parameters for spatial sigma, range sigma, and window size settings. Additional parameters manage edge detection threshold and iteration control. The output shows reduced noise while maintaining sharp edges and important image structures. This operation is crucial in medical imaging for detail preservation, computational photography for noise reduction, face recognition for preprocessing, HDR imaging for tone mapping, and scientific visualization where edge preservation is critical. It enables sophisticated noise reduction with excellent feature preservation.

median_filter.title: Median Filter
median_filter.description: Median filtering is a nonlinear operation that effectively reduces impulse noise while preserving edges. The input image requires parameters for window size, center weight factor, and iteration count settings. Additional parameters control adaptive threshold values and output blending options. The resulting image shows significantly reduced salt-and-pepper noise while maintaining edge sharpness. This operation is vital in medical imaging for artifact removal, astronomical imaging for cosmic ray removal, document processing for scan cleanup, industrial inspection for defect detection, and restoration of damaged images. It provides robust noise reduction for images affected by impulse noise.

wiener_filter.title: Wiener Filter
wiener_filter.description: Wiener filtering is a statistical image restoration operation that optimally reduces noise based on local image statistics. The input image requires parameters for noise estimation, local window size, and SNR threshold settings. Additional parameters manage frequency response and regularization factors. The output shows reduced noise with optimal preservation of image features based on signal-to-noise characteristics. This operation is essential in medical imaging for optimal noise reduction, astronomical imaging for signal recovery, microscopy for image enhancement, scientific imaging for data restoration, and professional photography for noise management. It provides statistically optimal noise reduction.

deblocking.title: Deblocking
deblocking.description: Deblocking is a specialized image enhancement operation that reduces artifacts from lossy compression methods. The input image requires parameters for block size detection, filtering strength, and edge preservation threshold. Additional parameters control artifact detection sensitivity and smoothing methods. The output shows reduced blocking artifacts while maintaining image detail and texture. This operation is crucial in video processing for compression artifact reduction, digital broadcasting for quality enhancement, streaming media optimization, forensic image analysis for detail recovery, and general image quality improvement. It enables improved visual quality for compressed digital content.

motion_deblurring.title: Motion Deblurring
motion_deblurring.description: Motion deblurring is a specialized image restoration operation that corrects blur caused by relative motion between camera and subject during exposure. Input parameters include the blurred image, motion path estimation (direction and magnitude), and exposure time information. The operation produces a sharpened image with reduced motion artifacts through deconvolution algorithms. Additional parameters control point spread function estimation, noise suppression, and ringing artifact reduction. Key processing settings include iteration count, convergence criteria, and edge preservation factors. This technique finds critical applications in surveillance systems for license plate recognition, sports photography for action shot recovery, medical imaging for patient movement compensation, astronomical imaging for telescope motion correction, and forensic analysis for evidence enhancement. It enables the recovery of sharp images from motion-blurred captures, improving detail visibility and recognition capabilities.

optical_deblurring.title: Optical Deblurring
optical_deblurring.description: Optical deblurring is an advanced image restoration operation targeting blur caused by defocus or lens imperfections. The input requires a blurred image and parameters defining the defocus blur kernel (circle of confusion), focal distance estimation, and lens characteristics. Output is a restored image with improved focus and detail definition. Essential parameters include point spread function modeling, depth estimation, and artifact suppression settings. The operation manages boundary conditions, noise amplification, and convergence control. This technique is vital in microscopy for extending depth of field, medical imaging for focus correction, astronomical imaging for atmospheric distortion compensation, industrial inspection for defect detection through protective barriers, and professional photography for post-capture focus adjustment. It enables the recovery of sharp images from optically degraded captures.

nonlinear_deblurring.title: Nonlinear Deblurring
nonlinear_deblurring.description: Nonlinear deblurring is a sophisticated image restoration operation that addresses complex blur patterns caused by nonlinear camera or object motion. Input includes the blurred image and parameters for nonlinear motion modeling, trajectory estimation, and spatially varying blur kernels. The operation outputs a restored image with reduced complex motion artifacts. Critical parameters include motion path segmentation, local blur estimation, and adaptive deconvolution settings. Additional controls manage spatial coherence, temporal consistency, and artifact suppression. This technique is essential in aerial imaging for platform motion compensation, autonomous vehicle vision systems, handheld device photography, sports action photography, and surveillance systems with complex object tracking. It enables effective restoration of images affected by complex motion patterns.

blind_deconvolution.title: Blind Deconvolution
blind_deconvolution.description: Blind deconvolution is an advanced image restoration operation that simultaneously estimates the blur kernel and recovers the sharp image without prior knowledge of the degradation process. Input consists of the blurred image with parameters for initial kernel estimation and regularization settings. Output includes both the estimated blur kernel and restored image. Key parameters control iterative optimization, convergence criteria, and noise handling. The operation manages edge preservation, artifact suppression, and local adaptation settings. This technique is crucial in astronomical imaging for atmospheric turbulence correction, medical imaging for motion artifact reduction, forensic image analysis, microscopy for automated focus correction, and general photography enhancement. It provides robust image restoration when blur characteristics are unknown.

turbulence_deblurring.title: Turbulence Deblurring
turbulence_deblurring.description: Turbulence deblurring is a specialized image restoration operation designed to correct distortions caused by atmospheric turbulence in long-distance imaging. Input requires sequences of turbulence-affected images and parameters for atmospheric condition modeling and temporal correlation estimation. Output provides a restored image with reduced atmospheric distortion effects. Critical parameters include turbulence strength estimation, frame selection criteria, and multi-frame registration settings. The operation manages temporal averaging, lucky imaging selection, and detail preservation. This technique is essential in long-range surveillance systems, astronomical imaging through atmosphere, aerial reconnaissance, maritime observation systems, and heat-affected industrial monitoring. It enables clear imaging through turbulent atmospheric conditions.

local_stabilization.title: Local Stabilization
local_stabilization.description: Local stabilization is a targeted video processing operation that stabilizes specific regions or objects within a frame while maintaining natural motion elsewhere. Input requires video frames and region selection parameters for stabilization focus. Output provides video with steady selected regions while preserving surrounding motion. Essential parameters include region tracking methods, motion compensation settings, and border handling options. The operation manages temporal consistency, spatial coherence, and frame composition. This technique is vital in sports broadcast for player tracking, medical procedures for surgical area stabilization, microscopy for specimen observation, industrial inspection for defect tracking, and surveillance systems for object monitoring. It enables focused stabilization of specific image areas while maintaining context.

global_stabilization.title: Global Stabilization
global_stabilization.description: Global stabilization is a comprehensive video processing operation that reduces overall camera shake and unwanted motion across entire frames. Input consists of video sequences and parameters for motion estimation and compensation across the full frame. Output provides smoothly stabilized video with consistent frame alignment. Critical parameters include global motion modeling, frame registration methods, and border handling settings. The operation manages acceleration smoothing, horizon correction, and frame composition. This technique is essential in drone videography for steady aerial shots, handheld video recording, vehicle-mounted cameras for smooth capture, architectural documentation, and virtual reality content creation. It enables professional-quality video stabilization for improved viewing experience.

perspective_registration.title: Perspective Registration
perspective_registration.description: Perspective registration is an advanced image alignment operation that corrects geometric differences between multiple views of the same scene. Input requires multiple images of a scene from different viewpoints and parameters for geometric transformation estimation. Output provides aligned images with consistent perspective projection. Key parameters include feature matching methods, transformation model selection, and interpolation settings. The operation manages multi-view geometry, outlier rejection, and blend optimization. This technique is crucial in 3D reconstruction from multiple views, panorama creation, medical image fusion, architectural documentation, and surveillance system integration. It enables consistent scene analysis across multiple viewpoints.

temporal_smoothing.title: Temporal Smoothing
temporal_smoothing.description: Temporal smoothing is an advanced video enhancement operation that reduces noise by intelligently combining information from multiple consecutive frames. Input requires a sequence of video frames and parameters for temporal alignment and weight distribution. Output provides noise-reduced frames with preserved motion detail. Essential parameters include temporal window size, motion estimation settings, and blend weight calculation methods. The operation manages frame registration, artifact suppression, and detail preservation. This technique is crucial in low-light video recording, medical fluoroscopy for dose reduction, surveillance systems for improved visibility, microscopy for live specimen imaging, and broadcast quality enhancement. It enables improved video quality through intelligent frame combination.

motion_smoothing.title: Motion Smoothing
motion_smoothing.description: Motion smoothing is a sophisticated video processing operation that reduces noise while specifically preserving motion integrity and preventing motion artifacts. Input consists of video sequences and parameters for motion vector estimation and compensation. Output provides smoothed video with clean motion representation and minimal halos. Critical parameters include motion field estimation, adaptive temporal filtering, and artifact prevention settings. The operation manages object boundary detection, occlusion handling, and temporal consistency. This technique is essential in sports broadcast for clear motion rendering, medical imaging for dynamic studies, high-speed video analysis, quality control systems for moving objects, and professional video post-processing. It enables high-quality video enhancement with preserved motion characteristics.

frame_averaging.title: Frame Averaging
frame_averaging.description: Frame averaging is a fundamental multi-frame processing operation that combines multiple images of the same scene to reduce random noise. Input requires a sequence of aligned frames and parameters for temporal weight distribution and registration methods. Output provides a single composite image with improved signal-to-noise ratio. Key parameters include frame alignment precision, outlier rejection criteria, and weight calculation methods. The operation manages exposure variations, motion compensation, and detail preservation. This technique is vital in astronomical imaging for weak signal detection, medical imaging for dose reduction, scientific photography for noise reduction, industrial inspection for improved detection, and night photography for clean images. It enables significant noise reduction through statistical combination of multiple frames.

super_resolution.title: Super Resolution
super_resolution.description: Super resolution is an advanced multi-frame processing operation that combines multiple low-resolution images to create a higher-resolution output. Input requires sequences of slightly shifted low-resolution frames and parameters for sub-pixel registration and reconstruction methods. Output provides an enhanced resolution image with improved detail visibility. Critical parameters include motion estimation accuracy, reconstruction algorithm selection, and artifact suppression settings. The operation manages sub-pixel alignment, information fusion, and detail enhancement. This technique is crucial in satellite imaging for improved ground sampling, surveillance systems for detail recovery, medical imaging for enhanced visualization, scientific imaging for resolution enhancement, and forensic analysis for evidence examination. It enables resolution improvement beyond single-frame limitations.
